haiku-low.q1: The API checks reports.row_count: 10,000 or fewer streams the CSV directly with 200. Above 10,000 returns 202 with an export record, built in the background and emailed as a link.
haiku-low.q2: The API returns the existing queued or running export record instead of creating a new one. A unique index allows only one active export per user per report.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours. The bucket lifecycle rule deletes the stored file 7 days after creation. No cleanup job exists.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, 60s then 300s apart. After the last fails, the record becomes failed and the user gets a report_export_failed email.
haiku-low.q5: The read replica only, never the primary database.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row, the only source of truth. The page polls exports/latest on load and every 5 seconds while queued or running, so reopening shows it.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000 rows at a time by row_id, holds one roughly 8 MB buffer, and uploads a part whenever it fills, so memory stays small. The document does not state timing for 2 million rows.
haiku-low.q8: Written parts stay in an unfinished multipart upload, never visible; a raised error aborts it, and the bucket discards leftovers. The next attempt restarts from the beginning with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: Stored in the report_exports filters and cols columns, copied from the page URL at click time. The job payload holds only export_id, so the job loads them from the record.
haiku-low.q10: The unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The second insert is rejected, and the API returns the existing record.
haiku-low.q11: complete_multipart must succeed, then the signed URL is built. If the job reruns for a record not queued or running, such as done or failed, it stops without sending anything.
haiku-low.q12: The download breaks and the user must click again. Nothing is stored, and no record or job is involved.

sonnet.q1: The API reads reports.row_count on click. 10,000 or fewer (small): 200 with text/csv streamed as the response, with a download header. Above 10,000 (large; unfiltered total is the only test, so filtered exports of large reports still use the job): 202 with a JSON export record, built in the background and emailed as a link.
sonnet.q2: The unique index on (user_id, report_id) for queued/running status rejects the new insert, so the API returns the existing active export record instead of creating a new one or enqueuing a job.
sonnet.q3: The signed link works for 24 hours (86400 s). The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation. No cleanup job is built.
sonnet.q4: At most 3 attempts (waits of 60 s then 300 s between). After the last fails (at worst about 1.5 hours after the click), on_final_failure sets the record to failed and sends the email report_export_failed. The page shows failed, and a new click is no longer blocked. No emails are sent for retried attempts.
sonnet.q5: The read replica only, never the primary (both the small path and the job read from the replica).
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table (the export record is the only source of truth). The page polls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load and every 5 s while status is queued or running. Reopening later works the same way because the record is in the database. Failed polls are ignored and retried.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads rows from the replica 5,000 at a time by row_id (keyset), holds one ~8 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, so memory stays small regardless of report size. It writes the header first, then calls complete_multipart at the end.
sonnet.q8: Nothing is visible, because the file only appears at complete_multipart. If the handler raises, it aborts its multipart upload. If the worker dies or times out, nothing aborts, but the unfinished upload is never visible and the bucket discards it after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts from the beginning (step 5) with a new upload, not resuming where the last one stopped.
sonnet.q9: They are copied from the page URL at click time into the filters and cols columns of the report_exports record. The job payload is only the export_id, and the job loads the record to get the stored filters and columns.
sonnet.q10: The unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running; the insert that loses is rejected and the API returns the existing record.
sonnet.q11: complete_multipart must have finished (file visible) and the signed URL been built before send_email. The email comes before the record is set to done. If the job runs again, it loads the record and stops if the status is not queued or running (e.g. done from a repeated delivery, or failed). If the final write failed after the email, the retry may send a second email and replace the file (both links point to the same key).
sonnet.q12: The download is broken and the user clicks again. No record, job or stored data exists for the small path.
